title: Reference and Master Data

toc.title: Data Governance for Reference and Master Data

html:
1Definition and Goals

Reference Data: Any data used to characterize or classify other data, or to relate data to information beyond the boundaries of the enterprise.

Master Data: Data about business entities (customers, products, employees, locations) that provide context for transactions; represents the most critical shared data across the enterprise.

MDM (Master Data Management) — Gartner Definition: "A technology-enabled discipline in which business and IT work together to ensure uniformity, accuracy, stewardship, semantic consistency, and accountability for the enterprise's official shared master data assets."

3 Goals:

  1. Ensure organization has access to accurate, complete, consistent Reference and Master Data
  2. Enable sharing and use of reference and master data across the enterprise
  3. Reduce risks and costs by managing this critical data with proper stewardship

2Business Drivers

  • Reduce inconsistency in reporting due to multiple versions of critical data
  • Improve data quality of customer, product, and other key entities
  • Support regulatory compliance
  • Enable better decision-making with consistent, accurate master data
  • Support data integration and interoperability
  • Reduce redundancy and cost of managing duplicated data

3Reference Data

Definition and Types

Reference data is organized into domains — sets of values used to classify or categorize.

Chisholm's 6-Layer Reference Data Taxonomy:

Layer Description
1. Internal Reference Data Created and maintained within the enterprise (e.g., department codes, cost center codes)
2. Industry Reference Data Standards established by industry groups (e.g., SIC codes, SWIFT codes)
3. National Reference Data Standards defined by national bodies (e.g., state codes, zip codes)
4. International Reference Data Standards defined by international bodies (e.g., ISO country codes, ISO currency codes)
5. Third-Party Reference Data Commercially available reference data (e.g., D&B DUNS numbers)
6. Reference Data Derived from Other Reference Data Created by combining/transforming existing reference data

Reference Data Types (Complexity Spectrum)

Type Description
Lists Simple enumerated values (e.g., status codes: Active, Inactive)
Cross-Reference Tables Map values between two or more classification systems
Taxonomies Hierarchical classification of values
Ontologies Most complex; networks of concepts and relationships

ICD Medical Code Example

  • ICD-9 — approximately 13,000 diagnostic codes
  • ICD-10 — approximately 68,000 diagnostic codes (expanded for greater specificity)

4Master Data

Key Characteristics

  • Represents the most important shared entities in the enterprise
  • Provides context for transactional data
  • Managed across multiple systems; must be consistent
  • Examples: Customer, Product, Employee, Location, Account, Supplier

Master Data Domains (Common)

  • Party — Person, Organization, Customer, Employee, Supplier
  • Product / Item
  • Financial — Account, Cost Center, General Ledger codes
  • Location — Address, Geography
  • Asset
  • Contract / Policy
  • Rule
  • Concept (e.g., industry classifications)

5Entity Resolution

Definition: Process of identifying, matching, and linking records that refer to the same real-world entity.

Two Matching Approaches:

Approach Description
Deterministic (Rules-Based) Uses exact or near-exact matching rules; high precision; requires clean data
Probabilistic (Statistical) Uses statistical weights to score match likelihood; handles data inconsistencies

Three Matching Workflows

Workflow Description
Duplicate Identification Find records representing same entity; mark duplicates without changing source systems
Match and Link Identify matches; link records to a "golden record" without consolidating
Match and Merge Identify matches; merge into single consolidated "golden record"

Golden Record / Best Version of Truth: The authoritative, consolidated record created from matched records.

6MDM Architecture Types (3 Sharing Architectures)

Architecture Description Key Characteristics
Registry (Index) Maintains index of master data locations; does not store master data itself; links to source systems Minimally invasive; no data movement; sources remain authoritative
Transaction Hub Central master data hub; all transactions go through hub; hub is system of record Strong data governance; single point of control; complex to implement
Consolidated (Repository) Physical consolidated copy of master data; synchronized periodically Better for analytics; not always real-time; may have latency
Note

Some sources also list Coexistence (hybrid) and Centralized as additional variants.

7MDM Implementation Styles

Style Description
Registry As above — index approach
Consolidation Physical merged copy
Coexistence Multiple authoritative sources; synchronization between them
Transaction Hub All transactions validated against hub
Centralized One system is the single source of truth for all consumers

8Data Governance for Reference and Master Data

Stewardship Responsibilities

  • Define and manage reference data domains
  • Resolve conflicts between different classification schemes
  • Approve changes to reference data values
  • Manage hierarchies and relationships

Reference Data Change Management

  • Changes to reference data values must be managed as formal changes
  • Historical values must be preserved for backward compatibility
  • Effective-dated records to track value changes over time

Master Data Governance

  • Assign data stewards per master data domain
  • Define system of record for each attribute
  • Manage data quality rules
  • Monitor matching rules and golden record creation

9Activities

Activity 1: Define Reference Data Strategy

  • Assess current reference data sources and quality
  • Define domains needing management
  • Identify cross-reference needs between systems

Activity 2: Define Master Data Management Strategy

  • Assess current state across systems
  • Select MDM architecture (registry, transaction hub, consolidated)
  • Define scope and priorities

Activity 3: Identify Reference Data Sources

  • Inventory all sources of reference data
  • Identify external standard sources
  • Determine internal vs. external governance

Activity 4: Establish Reference Data Governance

  • Assign stewards for each domain
  • Define change management processes
  • Establish approval workflows

Activity 5: Implement MDM Solution

  • Implement entity resolution (matching rules)
  • Create golden records
  • Integrate with source systems
  • Monitor data quality

10Tools and Techniques

MDM Tools

  • Entity resolution engines (deterministic + probabilistic matching)
  • Data quality tools (profiling, cleansing, standardization)
  • Data integration tools (ETL/ELT for loading master data)
  • Workflow tools (stewardship approvals)

Reference Data Management Tools

  • Reference data repositories
  • Business glossary tools
  • Metadata repositories

11Metrics

6 Metric Categories for Reference and Master Data:

Category Examples
Completeness Percentage of required reference data values present
Coverage Percentage of enterprise entities with master records
Quality Percentage of records meeting quality thresholds
Matching Precision and recall of entity matching
Timeliness Currency of master data relative to source changes
Usage Number of systems consuming master data

12Practice Q&A

Q1: What is the Gartner definition of MDM? A: "A technology-enabled discipline in which business and IT work together to ensure uniformity, accuracy, stewardship, semantic consistency, and accountability for the enterprise's official shared master data assets."

Q2: What are the 6 layers of Chisholm's Reference Data Taxonomy? A: Internal, Industry, National, International, Third-Party, Derived from other reference data.

Q3: What is a "golden record"? A: The authoritative, consolidated record created from matched master data records; also called "best version of truth."

Q4: What are the two entity resolution approaches? A: Deterministic (rules-based matching — exact/near-exact rules) and Probabilistic (statistical weights to score match likelihood).

Q5: What are the 3 matching workflows? A: Duplicate Identification, Match and Link, Match and Merge.

Q6: What are the 3 primary MDM sharing architectures? A: Registry (index only), Transaction Hub (central control), Consolidated (physical copy).

Q7: What is the key difference between Registry and Consolidated MDM architectures? A: Registry maintains an index/pointer to master data in source systems without storing data itself; Consolidated physically stores a merged copy of master data.

Q8: What are the reference data types from simple to complex? A: Lists, Cross-Reference Tables, Taxonomies, Ontologies.

Q9: How many ICD-9 vs. ICD-10 codes exist? A: ICD-9 ≈ 13,000 codes; ICD-10 ≈ 68,000 codes.

Q10: What is the difference between Reference Data and Master Data? A: Reference Data classifies or characterizes other data (e.g., codes, categories); Master Data represents key business entities that provide context for transactions (e.g., customer, product).

Q11: What are common Master Data domains? A: Party (customer, employee, supplier), Product, Financial (accounts), Location, Asset, Contract.

Q12: What is entity resolution? A: Process of identifying, matching, and linking records that refer to the same real-world entity.

Q13: What is "coexistence" in MDM? A: Multiple authoritative source systems co-exist; master data synchronized between them (hybrid approach).

Q14: What are 3 typical stewardship responsibilities for reference data? A: Define and manage domains, resolve classification conflicts, approve changes to reference data values.

Q15: What is the primary business risk of poor master data management? A: Inconsistent reporting, conflicting versions of critical entities, poor data quality affecting business decisions, and regulatory compliance risks.

13Quick Reference

Concept Key Fact
Reference Data Classifies/characterizes other data; organized into domains
Master Data Business entities providing context for transactions
MDM Gartner Definition Ensures uniformity, accuracy, stewardship, semantic consistency
Chisholm 6 Layers Internal, Industry, National, International, Third-Party, Derived
Reference Data Types Lists → Cross-Ref → Taxonomies → Ontologies
ICD-9 ~13,000 codes
ICD-10 ~68,000 codes
Deterministic Matching Exact/near-exact rules; high precision; clean data needed
Probabilistic Matching Statistical weights; handles inconsistencies
3 Matching Workflows Duplicate ID, Match+Link, Match+Merge
Golden Record Authoritative consolidated master record
MDM Registry Index only; minimally invasive; sources remain authoritative
MDM Transaction Hub Central hub; all transactions go through it
MDM Consolidated Physical copy; better for analytics
6 Metric Categories Completeness, Coverage, Quality, Matching, Timeliness, Usage
